section_summary: This section concerns defaulted Japanese government, municipal, and government-guaranteed bonds held by American and Canadian investors. The State Department records individual holdings, explains the limits of its assistance, and discusses claims, trading restrictions, bond security, and possible peace-treaty treatment. It also contains a Foreign Bondholders Protective Council policy letter and correspondence about obtaining updated Japanese economic statistics.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japanese bondholder
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its bondholder policy and requests details of bonds and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Concludes a reply begun before this section, requesting bond and citizenship details for possible future consideration.

subfiles.title: Instruction to American Mission, Ottawa, concerning MacEwan
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Ottawa
subfiles.about: The mission is asked to transmit the Department's reply to Keith MacEwan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards MacEwan's inquiry and the Department's reply for delivery.

subfiles.title: Keith MacEwan inquiry about Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: MacEwan reports two Japanese bonds whose interest has gone unpaid since the war.
subfiles.summary: Reports two $100 Japanese bonds and asks about recovery of unpaid interest and principal.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for Tokyo despatch 1451
subfiles.about: A record copy replaces the unreturned action copy of a Tokyo despatch.
subfiles.summary: Designates the following despatch as the record copy.

subfiles.title: Request concerning specific Japanese dollar bond issues
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tokyo forwards Japanese Finance Ministry information requested by the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
subfiles.summary: Reports that occupation authorities obtained information on specified Japanese dollar issues; completed forms and a Council letter are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Reply to Gertrude Herz
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Herz's inquiry about Japanese government and Yokohama bonds.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Department's limited role, points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and requests bond and citizenship particulars for its records.

subfiles.title: Gertrude Herz inquiry
subfiles.about: Herz asks how American owners of Japanese bonds can safeguard or register claims.
subfiles.summary: Asks what protection and claim registration the Department provides.

subfiles.title: Sumajiro Harada inquiry
subfiles.about: Harada asks about the status of Tokyo Electric bonds.
subfiles.summary: Requests information after referral by the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Judge O'Neill bond inquiry
subfiles.about: O'Neill asks how to protect claims on his Japanese bond and his wife's Berlin bond.
subfiles.summary: Describes two defaulted bonds and asks whether further action is needed.

subfiles.title: Reply to Judge O'Neill
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Financial Affairs
subfiles.about: The Department responds to O'Neill's inquiries about defaulted foreign bonds.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Department's position on foreign bonds and directs attention to the bondholder representative body.

subfiles.title: Banque Belge acknowledgment
subfiles.from: Banque Belge pour l'Étranger, New York Agency
subfiles.about: The bank acknowledges a State Department letter and says it is contacting Belgium's representative in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt and reports contact with the Belgian diplomatic representative.

subfiles.title: Representative Rogers forwards Neesen inquiry
subfiles.about: Rogers requests advice on a constituent's Tokyo Electric bond interest.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Dr. Neesen's letter and asks for advice and return of the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Victor Neesen letter to Representative Rogers
subfiles.about: Neesen asks why funds deposited for interest on his Tokyo Electric bonds have not been released.
subfiles.summary: Seeks release of prewar interest funds held by the Alien Property Custodian.

subfiles.title: Referral of Neesen inquiry to Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: State refers Rogers's and Neesen's letters for appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the bond-interest inquiry to the office responsible for the held funds.

subfiles.title: Reply to Representative Rogers
subfiles.from: Charles E. Bohlen, Department of State
subfiles.about: State tells Rogers that Neesen's matter has been referred to the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.summary: Explains the office's jurisdiction and confirms referral of the letters.

subfiles.title: London report on parliamentary discussion of Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: The embassy reports British parliamentary exchanges on Japanese bondholders and debt service.
subfiles.summary: Quotes questions and the Chancellor's reply: bondholders' rights will figure in peace discussions, but Japan's payments position makes early debt service unlikely.

subfiles.title: London report on Financial Times editorial
subfiles.about: The embassy transmits British press commentary on Japanese bond prospects.
subfiles.summary: Relays a Financial Times editorial assessing British policy, Japan's capacity to pay, and the likely influence of U.S. settlement terms.

subfiles.title: Reply to Douglas Graham
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State responds to Graham's holdings of Great Consolidated Electric Power dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Records his holdings, explains the Department's limited assistance and the Council's role, and asks for acquisition, interest, and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Douglas Graham bond letter
subfiles.about: Graham reports five $1,000 Great Consolidated Electric Power bonds in a claim filed with Alien Property.
subfiles.summary: Asks about his five bonds and an expected claim receipt.

subfiles.title: MacEwan follow-up on citizenship
subfiles.about: MacEwan asks whether his Canadian citizenship prevents him from making a claim.
subfiles.summary: Says he can supply the requested bond details except American citizenship and seeks clarification.

subfiles.title: Council policy letter on Japanese governmental dollar debt
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, Foreign Bondholders Protective Council
subfiles.about: The Council urges full service and protection of Japanese public and guaranteed dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Estimates roughly $68 million of Japanese governmental dollar debt outside Japan and about $4 million in annual interest. It urges full payment through a peace settlement and describes disrupted fiscal agencies, seized service funds, changed trustees, wartime conversions, and canceled mortgage liens. It also discusses British policy and early consultation with bondholders.

subfiles.title: Schedule of Japanese dollar bond issues
subfiles.about: A table lists fourteen Japanese national, municipal, and guaranteed corporate dollar issues.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates issue dates, maturities, outstanding principal, estimated holdings outside Japan, annual interest, fiscal agents, and trustees.

subfiles.title: L. E. Colgrove inquiry
subfiles.about: Colgrove asks whether two inherited Imperial Japanese Government bonds retain value.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the inherited 1924 bonds and attached coupons and requests a valuation.

subfiles.title: Reply to L. E. Colgrove
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State explains why it cannot value Colgrove's bonds and offers to record his holdings.
subfiles.summary: Cites the halt in Japanese bond transactions, explains the Department's policy and the Council's role, and requests citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Reply to Joseph Padolino
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State answers Padolino's question about disposing of Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Explains the trading halt and uncertain future of the bonds, records his holdings, and notes possible debt claims with the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Routing slip
subfiles.about: An urgent internal routing slip accompanies the Padolino correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Marks the material urgent for the Legal Adviser.

subfiles.title: Joseph Padolino inquiry
subfiles.about: Padolino seeks advice on redeeming Japanese government bonds or obtaining overdue interest.
subfiles.summary: The elderly retired holder asks whether he can redeem his bonds or collect coupons.

subfiles.title: Moody's request for updated Japan statistics
subfiles.from: J. S. Porter, Moody's Investors Service
subfiles.about: Moody's requests updated Japanese public debt, budget, trade, and other statistics for its manual.
subfiles.summary: Sends manual excerpts and asks that updated material reach Moody's by August 15.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Moody's
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Moody's request and forwards its excerpts to the Political Adviser for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Promises to seek revision of the manual excerpts in Japan.

subfiles.title: Further reply to Moody's
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Department of State
subfiles.about: State redirects Moody's request for Japanese statistics to the Army Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Army reporting channel and apologizes for the delay.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Political Adviser on Moody's request
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: State asks the mission to arrange revision of Moody's Japan manual excerpts.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Moody's letter and excerpts with its August 15 deadline.

subfiles.title: Ottawa instruction forwarding MacEwan correspondence
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Ottawa
subfiles.about: State asks the mission to deliver its latest reply to MacEwan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses MacEwan's follow-up letter and the Department's response.

subfiles.title: Reply to Keith MacEwan
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State clarifies how Canadian citizenship affects MacEwan's Japanese bond interests.
subfiles.summary: Says Council recommendations cover holders regardless of citizenship, while State represents U.S. citizens; repayment remains uncertain.

subfiles.title: Gertrude Working bond particulars
subfiles.about: Working supplies details of her inherited Ujigawa Electric Power bond and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Records acquisition, face value, last interest payment, maturity, and citizenship by birth.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Gertrude Working
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State confirms Working's bond details will be filed.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt and placement of her information in Department records.

subfiles.title: W. D. Black inquiry to Treasury
subfiles.about: Black asks whether his Tokyo and Yokohama bonds may eventually pay principal.
subfiles.summary: Describes two government-guaranteed municipal bonds and requests Treasury's opinion.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Black inquiry
subfiles.about: Treasury sends Black's Japanese bond inquiry to State for reply.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Black's letter and an acknowledgment copy.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to Black
subfiles.about: Treasury tells Black that State will consider his bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Confirms referral to State's Division of Financial Affairs.

subfiles.title: State reply to W. D. Black
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State responds to Black's Tokyo and Yokohama bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Department's policy and the Council's role, requests fuller bond and citizenship information, and points to possible Alien Property claims.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Norman Webster
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Webster's additional details on City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that the information will be recorded for possible future use.

subfiles.title: Norman Webster bond particulars
subfiles.about: Webster supplies purchase and citizenship details for his City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: Gives acquisition and citizenship particulars and asks whether to contact the London bondholders' organization.

subfiles.title: Ralph Everett bond particulars
subfiles.about: Everett lists his Oriental Development bonds, purchase details, unpaid interest, and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Supplies the information State requested for its bondholder records.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Ralph Everett
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State confirms Everett's Oriental Development bond details will be filed.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the particulars for possible future consideration.

subfiles.title: Reply to Emmy Lou Port
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State responds belatedly to Port's inquiry about Oriental Development bonds.
subfiles.summary: Offers to record her holdings if she is an American citizen, explains State's limited role and the Council's work, and asks for citizenship information.

subfiles.title: Reply to Harris Trust on Nippon Electric mortgage liens
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State reports its request for occupation authorities' views on restoring Nippon Electric mortgage liens.
subfiles.summary: Says a response is pending and suggests that Harris Trust contact the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Harris Trust renewed request
subfiles.from: F. O. Mann, Harris Trust and Savings Bank
subfiles.about: Harris Trust asks State to protect Nippon Electric bondholders through restoration of canceled liens.
subfiles.summary: Reports a possible Japanese willingness to reinstate mortgage liens if the U.S. government requests it.

subfiles.title: Harris Trust letter on Nippon Electric defaults
subfiles.from: F. O. Mann, Harris Trust and Savings Bank
subfiles.about: The bank details wartime changes to the Nippon Electric bond indenture and seeks protection for holders.
subfiles.summary: Explains the original mortgage, later property transfers and guarantees, cessation of payments, wartime yen conversion, government assumption of externally held bonds, and cancellation of the mortgage. The bank rejects these changes as violations of bondholders' rights and seeks restoration, including through the peace treaty.

subfiles.title: First National Bank of Elgin inquiry
subfiles.about: An estate executor asks whether State requires a filing for a Taiwan Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies James W. Lynch's bond and prior Alien Property claim, then asks about additional forms.

subfiles.title: Reply to A. J. Wilkening
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Financial Affairs
subfiles.about: State replies concerning the Lynch estate's Taiwan Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Offers to record the holding, explains its limited assistance to bondholders and the Council's role, and says any later steps will be publicized.

subfiles.title: Required Economic Reporting
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Japan mission asks how to obtain occupation data for Moody's and other economic reports.
subfiles.summary: The mission says occupation headquarters will not provide extensive data for reports requested outside Army channels. It distinguishes confidential policy analysis from routine statistical reporting and proposes that the Army request such reports directly from occupation staff.

subfiles.title: Distribution of SCAP Reports
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The memorandum sets routing rules for requests for occupation reports.
subfiles.summary: Directs requests from outside the theater through the War Department and local requests through the statistical section.

subfiles.title: Reply to Clarence Leonard
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State supplies a delayed substantive reply about Leonard's Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Apologizes for the delay, describes State's limited role and the Council's work, and offers to record Leonard's holdings for future consideration.

subfiles.title: Reply to A. H. Sherwin
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State answers questions about trading Japanese bonds and commercial trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Says securities trading restrictions remain and directs commercial trade inquiries to the Department of Commerce.

subfiles.title: A. H. Sherwin inquiry
subfiles.about: Sherwin asks about Japanese bond trading restrictions and trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Department's view on reopening bond trading and permitting commercial dealings.

subfiles.title: Reply to Edwin J. Paull
subfiles.about: State begins a delayed reply about Paull's two Ujigawa Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: Explains the trading halt and begins stating the Department's policy on defaulted government-guaranteed bonds; the letter continues beyond this section.
